Ekipazh: Russia’s top-secret nuclear-powered satellite   

#satellite #weapons 

This nuclear-powered satellite is just one example; there are other classified systems above the “top secret” level that we will probably never know about.

Ekipazh is intended for space-based electronic warfare (EW), such as jamming or other electromagnetic attacks from orbit. This aligns with Russian military doctrine documents from around 2012–2016 that called for developing space EW capabilities by 2025, as well as statements from industry figures about "space-based armament systems" for future warfare.

Details about another system Plazma-A

Experimental Plasma-Cloud Generation for ASAT Defense

One of the key payloads on Plazma-A was Epikur (or Epicure), designed to generate artificial plasma clouds in space. The concept was defensive: release ionized gas (plasma) to create a temporary "shield" or cloud around friendly satellites.

Purpose: Mask or protect satellites from anti-satellite (ASAT) interceptors or sensors by:

Scattering/absorbing radar signals (similar to how plasma sheaths around reentering vehicles or hypersonic missiles can reduce radar cross-section).

Interfering with optical/infrared tracking.

Potentially disrupting directed-energy weapons or kinetic kill vehicles approaching through the plasma.
